chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: Ibn Abi Ya'fur asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was listening,
about the fasting person, does he pour medicine into his ear? He said: 'Yes, and he tastes the broth and he feeds the young bird.'
ai.seo_question: Does applying medicine to the ear break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that applying medicine to the ear does not break the fast, distinguishing it from actions that involve swallowing substantial nourishment. The Imam supports this ruling by drawing analogies to tasting food (*yadhawu al-marqa*) and feeding a young bird (*yazquq al-farxa*), which are permissible acts that do not nullify the fast due to the small quantity or lack of deep swallowing. This establishes a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding minor medical interventions during Ramadan.
